# DC renderer robustness & compliance hardening

## Context / Problem
The DC path shells out to pandoc per field. Two hazards from the DC experiment remain
in scope: (1) **pathological-input hang** — one corpus body spun pandoc's jira reader
13.5 min at 95.8% CPU, and pypandoc sets no timeout, so a single field can stall the
reconcile indefinitely; (2) **licence provenance** — pandoc is GPL and rides inside the
`pypandoc-binary` wheel, so its pin and licence must be recorded.

A third hazard, the ~0.3s/field subprocess spawn tax (~20 min of wall time on a large
serial reconcile), was originally to be addressed here by batching contiguous safe
units into one pandoc call. **That is now DESCOPED** — see "Descoped" below.

## Prior art / dependency boundaries (do NOT re-decide 271c's choices)
- **The renderer and its pandoc delivery are owned by 271c.** Story
  `[rebar:271c-e88f-3220-4c9b]` LANDED the pure renderer at
  `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (merged `cf5155e528`), with pandoc from the
  pinned **`pypandoc-binary==1.15` wheel** (bundled binary, **pandoc 3.6.1**) via a
  `wiki` extra, so no system pandoc is needed. This story hardens THAT module and pins
  THAT wheel; it adds no system pandoc and no `acli`-style version+sha binary pin.
- 271c leaves `WikiTextCodec` identity and `wiki_render.py` unreferenced by any codec op
  or live send path; all live wiring is the cutover story
  `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]`'s and is **out of scope here**.
- The change-gated "no-op → no pandoc spawn" property is that cutover story's `rich_sha`
  gate, not on `origin/main` and not this story's to add.

## Approach
- **Hard timeout + process-group reaping.** A plain `subprocess.run(timeout=)` reaps only
  the DIRECT child, so a jira-reader spinning at ~95.8% CPU (a pipe-holding grandchild)
  survives (bug d843, bpo-30154). So the renderer MUST NOT use pypandoc's high-level
  `convert_text`/`convert_file` API (no process handle): it locates pandoc via
  `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()`, builds its OWN
  `subprocess.Popen([pandoc_path, …], start_new_session=True)`, enforces the wall clock
  caller-side via `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` and, on
  `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, passes that `Popen` to **`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`**
  (`_proc.py:26`) — `killpg` SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL→bounded drain, already reused by the
  ACLI transport and grounding harness — killing the whole group. It kills/drains only
  AFTER a timeout is detected, so caller-side detection is required
  (`acli_subprocess.py`'s pattern). This REPLACES the landed `subprocess.run(timeout=30)`
  in `_convert` (`wiki_render.py`), which reaps only the direct child.
- **The timeout is a config key** (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default **10s**):
  >30× the observed ~0.3s/field render and ~80× below the 13.5-min hang;
  `grace`/`drain` reuse the ACLI caller's constants.
- **Fallback granularity is UNCHANGED — per unit.** On timeout or non-zero exit the unit
  degrades to its original Markdown verbatim (echo-safe), exactly as the landed
  `_render_unit` already does on conversion or preservation failure. One unit's failure
  never affects another, and no rendered output changes.
- **Compliance:** pin the wheel, create a repo-root `NOTICE` recording pandoc's GPL
  entry, and verify the pin in CI.

## Descoped: safe-run batching (operator decision, evidence-backed)
Batching maximal runs of contiguous safe units into one pandoc call was prototyped and
measured against the landed renderer over the committed 178-body corpus, and is
**removed from this story**:
- Ceiling is 233 runs vs 884 units = 74% fewer spawns, but **106 of 233 runs (46%) are a
  single unit**, so the ceiling is unreachable.
- Run-level fallback poisons a whole run on one bad fragment: **63/178 bodies (35%) lose
  richness**.
- Verify-then-accept with per-unit fallback keeps richness (157/178 identical) but yields
  only **12% fewer spawns**, since a failed batch pays for both attempts.
- **21/178 bodies still render DIFFERENTLY** even when a batch verifies: pandoc parses
  block boundaries relative to surrounding content, so concatenation is not equivalent to
  per-unit rendering.
~12% fewer spawns in exchange for changed output on ~12% of bodies is a bad trade, and a
silent rendering change is not something to ship. The spawn tax is properly addressed by
the cutover story's change-gated `rich_sha` skip, which avoids rendering unchanged bodies
at all. A follow-up idea ticket carries the 21-divergent-bodies analysis if spawn cost
matters after `rich_sha` lands.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — replace `_convert`'s `subprocess.run` with an
  own `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True)` over `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()`, the
  caller-side timeout, and `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`. Per-unit fallback behaviour
  and all rendered output stay byte-identical.
- `pyproject.toml` — pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel version (extends 271c's pin).
- config (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s). A `reconciler.*` key has a
  fixed multi-file surface (mirrors `reconciler.jira_cli_timeout`); update together:
  `_config_schema.py` — field `dc_pandoc_timeout_s: float = 10.0` on `ReconcilerConfig`
  + validator `_as_float(v, k, minimum=0.0)`; `_config_sources.py` — a
  `_CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES` alias only if a non-derived env name is wanted (else
  auto-derived `REBAR_RECONCILER_DC_PANDOC_TIMEOUT_S`);
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json` — deliberately REGENERATE (the guard
  `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` is removal-only, so it will NOT flag a new
  key's omission); `docs/config.md` — document it under `[tool.rebar.reconciler]`. A unit
  test mirrors `test_config_file_wiring.py`'s four-consumer pattern.
- CI workflow — verify the wheel pin (NOT an acli-style sha check).
- **`NOTICE` (NEW file, repo root)** — the repo has only `LICENSE` today and no
  SBOM/notice artifact, so this story CREATES `NOTICE` and records the wheel-bundled
  pandoc's GPL entry (name, version 3.6.1, licence, upstream) there.
- `tests/` — timeout, reaping and fallback tests over the vendored DC corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every pandoc invocation runs under a caller-side wall-clock timeout via
  `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` (config
  `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s — above the ~0.3s render, below the
  13.5-min hang); verified by `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back`.
- [ ] On `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` the whole process GROUP is reaped via
  `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`, so a CPU-spinning grandchild is killed rather than
  orphaned; verified by `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back` spawning a child that forks a
  spinning grandchild and asserting the group is gone.
- [ ] On timeout or non-zero exit the affected UNIT degrades to its original Markdown
  without raising and the render returns; verified by `test_dc_pandoc_error_degrades`.
- [ ] Rendered output is byte-identical to the landed renderer for the whole committed
  178-body corpus, proving this story changes robustness only, not rendering; verified by
  `test_dc_hardening_does_not_change_output`.
- [ ] `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` is reachable from config file and environment and
  documented; verified by a `test_config_file_wiring.py`-style four-consumer test plus
  the regenerated `tests/golden/config_surface.json`.
- [ ] The pandoc binary comes from the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pinned by version in
  `pyproject.toml` and the pin is verified in CI; verified by the CI wheel-pin check.
- [ ] The wheel-bundled pandoc's GPL licence is recorded in a NEW repo-root `NOTICE` file
  (only `LICENSE` exists today), naming pandoc, version 3.6.1 and its licence; verified
  by `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py`.
